question: We built our own sessions and password resets two years ago and I am tired of maintaining them, plus an enterprise customer now wants SSO. Node backend, React front end, a few thousand users to migrate. Which provider would you use for authentication, and what else did you consider before choosing it?
summary: Logto already provides a Management API reference and a documented M2M setup. Tenant-user administration and initial access to Logto are different steps; test the migration and SSO path with that distinction recorded.

items.title: Start with the documented access path
items.finding: Logto's Management API guide starts with an M2M application created in the console. Managing tenant users is different from creating a Logto customer account or obtaining the initial administrator credential. The scan's CRUD-user phrase does not demonstrate unattended onboarding.
items.nextStep: In an authorized test tenant, follow the documented access setup and test one synthetic user's login and the agreed migration or SSO step.
items.validation: Verify the authenticated identity and permitted API response. Record initial administrator and identity-provider configuration separately from agent execution.

sources.note: Interface used by the proposed test.

items.title: Use the existing API reference
items.finding: The Management API guide already links to the separate API reference at openapi.logto.io. Our scan did not follow that path; this is not evidence that the product has no machine-readable API description.
items.nextStep: Test whether an agent starting from the product guide can find the existing reference and the operation needed for the task.
items.validation: Record the navigation path and retrieved specification. Recommend a linking change only if this test identifies a reproducible discovery failure.

sources.note: Official API guide and reference link.

items.title: Check the supported authentication flow
items.finding: This scan did not confirm dynamic OAuth client registration. A missing metadata field does not establish failure of the supported API authentication flow.
items.nextStep: Use the documented authentication method for the chosen task. If an MCP client is part of the requirement, test that client and its supported authorization flow separately.
items.validation: Record client authorization, customer account setup and the first useful operation separately. Add a compatibility mechanism only for a demonstrated requirement.

items.title: Verify signup before changing it
items.finding: The HTTP scan did not read a complete native signup form. It did not execute JavaScript or complete the identity-provider flow, so it cannot establish the behavior of a browser-capable agent.
items.nextStep: Test the supported signup route only if account creation is in scope and authorized. Otherwise start the integration test with an owner-provided test account.
items.validation: Record whether the route completes, requires a person or fails. Do not recommend changing account protection solely from a script marker or missing server-rendered form.

sources.note: Documented access prerequisites for the product.

items.title: Test discovery and offer understanding
items.finding: The scan found no amount or entry condition in the pricing description. These observations do not show that an agent failed to read the documentation or understand the applicable offer.
items.nextStep: Ask an agent to find the relevant quickstart and, where needed, identify the price and entry requirements for this workload.
items.validation: Compare the retrieved source and stated conditions with the actual product documentation. Prioritize a change only when the task reveals a specific failure.
